messages.subject: Re: bootstrap script for 0.66 on Amazon Elastic MapReduce
messages.subject_clean: bootstrap script for 0.66 on Amazon Elastic MapReduce
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Found the solution to my problem. In my case it should be GFORTRAN=/
usr/lib/gcc/i486-linux-gnu/4.3/libgfortran* . Do not know if it can be
generalized for all though.

Yours
Bharath

On Aug 30, 8:29 pm, M Nakamura <masayang.mob...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Bharath,
>
> Obviously, the system was saying it couldn't find libgfortran.
>
> Which region are you using? My script is working on US-East.
>
> Yours,
>
> Masa Nakamura
>
>
>
>
>
>
>
> On Tue, Aug 30, 2011 at 2:56 AM, bharath raj <bharath...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi Masa Nakamura,
>
> > I followed the above steps on amazon emr and could execute this
> > successfully
> > $ elastic-mapreduce --create --alive --bootstrap-action s3://<your
> > bucket here>/bootstrap_0.66.sh <http://bootstrap_0.66.sh> --num-instances 5 --instance-type
> > m1.large
>
> > and created a job flow.
>
> > But when I ran this
> > $ elastic-mapreduce --ssh j-AABBCCDD
>
> > I encounter an error. The stderr log file says:
> > dpkg-preconfigure: unable to re-open stdin:
> > dpkg-preconfigure: unable to re-open stdin:
> > dpkg-preconfigure: unable to re-open stdin:
> > /bin/cp: cannot stat `/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/4.3/libgfortran*':
> > No such file or directory
>
> > Regards
> > Bharath
>
> > On Aug 23, 5:07 am, masayang <masayang.mob...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >> I updated the bootstrap script for 0.66.
>
> >> --begin
> >> #! /bin/bash
> >> set -e
>
> >> export HADOOP=/home/hadoop
>
> >> SOURCESLIST=sources.list
> >> APTDIR=/etc/apt
> >> CP=/bin/cp
> >> SUDO=/usr/bin/sudo
> >> APT=/usr/bin/apt-get
> >> WGET=/usr/bin/wget
> >> TAR=/bin/tar
> >> MAKE=/usr/bin/make
> >> R=/usr/bin/R
> >> LDCONFIG=/sbin/ldconfig
> >> CAT=/bin/cat
> >> CHOWN=/bin/chown
> >> LIBR=/usr/local/lib/R
> >> LIBDIR=/usr/lib
> >> GFORTRAN=/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/4.3/libgfortran*
>
> >> PROTOBUF_PATH=http://protobuf.googlecode.com/files/
> >> PROTOBUF=protobuf-2.4.1
> >> PROTOBUF_SRC=$PROTOBUF.tar.gz
>
> >> RHIPE_PATH=http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/download/
> >> RHIPE_SRC=Rhipe_0.66.tar.gz
>
> >> $CAT << EOF > $SOURCESLIST
> >> debhttp://http.us.debian.org/debian <http://http.us.debian.org/debian> stable         main contrib non-
> >> free
> >> debhttp://security.debian.org <http://security.debian.org>       lenny/updates  main contrib non-
> >> free
> >> debhttp://security.debian.org <http://security.debian.org>       stable/updates main contrib non-
> >> free
> >> EOF
>
> >> $SUDO $CP $SOURCESLIST $APTDIR/$SOURCESLIST
> >> $SUDO $APT update
> >> $SUDO $APT -y install r-base-dev
> >> $SUDO $APT -y install pkg-config
> >> $SUDO $APT -y install emacs ess
>
> >> $SUDO $CP $GFORTRAN $LIBDIR
>
> >> $WGET $PROTOBUF_PATH$PROTOBUF_SRC
> >> $TAR xvfz $PROTOBUF_SRC
> >> cd $PROTOBUF && ./configure && $MAKE && $SUDO $MAKE install && $SUDO
> >> $LDCONFIG
> >> $WGET $RHIPE_PATH$RHIPE_SRC
> >> $SUDO $CHOWN -R hadoop:hadoop $LIBR
> >> $R CMD INSTALL $RHIPE_SRC
>
> >> cd $HADOOP && $CAT << EOF >> .bashrc
> >> export HADOOP=/home/hadoop
> >> export HADOOP_BIN=/home/hadoop/bin
> >> EOF
>
> >> cd $HADOOP && $CAT << EOF >> install.R
> >> install.packages("biglm", repos="http://cran.r-project.org/")
> >> install.packages("multicore", repos="http://cran.r-project.org/")
> >> EOF
> >> $R CMD BATCH install.R
> >> --end
>
> >> How to use it?
>
> >> First of all, you needAmazonWeb Service account, then upload the
> >> script onto your S3 bucket. You also needelastic-mapreducecommand
> >> line tools.
>
> >> Following command will start Rhipe cluster with five m1.large
> >> instances.
>
> >> $elastic-mapreduce--create --alive --bootstrap-action s3://<your
> >> bucket here>/bootstrap_0.66.sh <http://bootstrap_0.66.sh> --num-instances 5 --instance-type
> >> m1.large
>
> >> The command will return the instance id like j-AABBCCDD. You can login
> >> to the cluster using this id.
>
> >> $elastic-mapreduce--ssh j-AABBCCDD
>
> >> From here, you can start your R session.
>
> >> Don't forget to terminate the cluster when you are done.
>
> >> $elastic-mapreduce--terminate j-AABBCCDD
>
> >> Enjoy.
>
> >> Masa Nakamura

messages.subject: Re: Problems with pkg-config
messages.body_plain:
Install pkg-config .
I have not found a way to build without pkg-config unless you unpackage the Rhipe package, edit the Makevars.in in R/src folder.

installed in user directory. No root privileges. Installing Rhipe and

Rhipe_0.66.tar.gz" on protobuf headers. Any suggestion/previous
experience?

cd ~/dev
wget http://protobuf.googlecode.com/files/protobuf-2.4.1.tar.gz
tar -xzvf protobuf-2.4.1.tar.gz
cd protobuf-2.4.1
./configure
make
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=/homes/max/dev/protobuf-2.4.1wget

2)
cd ~/dev
wget http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/download/Rhipe_0.66.tar.gz
tar -xzvf Rhipe_0.66.tar.gz
cd Rhipe
alias R='/homes/max/dev/R-2.13.1/bin/R'
export R_HOME=/homes/max/dev/R-2.13.1
./configure

cd ~/dev
